main_body: Round leafy tree canopy of clustered lobes on a brown trunk with a flared root base
top_band: Canopy lobes read as domed volumes with light-green highlights at the upper part of each lobe (rows ~1-10 at the top lobe) shading to dark green at the bottom; the trunk below has no top surface (organic form). Mid-column rows 22-40: light-mid green lobe tops grading into dark underside.
evidence: Organic canopy built from overlapping rounded lobes, each lit on top with a darker underside and dark shadow between the lobes and beneath the canopy, so it reads as a volume viewed from above and front. The trunk is a vertical column with a flared base, which is normal for a tree. There is no flat front elevation, no side face and no rim-only structure. The lobe tops are lighter and the undersides carry shadow, which satisfies the organic 3/4 reading.

style.evidence: The canopy has about 4 green steps (dark, mid, light, highlight) with scattered lighter and darker speckles, but the lobes are smooth and bulbous compared with the reference's leaf-cluster silhouettes, which carry per-leaf highlights and ragged edges. The outline is a very dark green-black that is almost neutral on the underside and bottom edge, giving a mild sticker look. The trunk is a fairly flat brown with a few vertical grain streaks and a simple flare, with no roots or branches visible, much thinner than the reference's rooted, branching trunks. Overall it is cleanly drawn but less rich and less textured than the Beodeul trees.
